summary: The note explores canning and fermenting as ways to preserve seasonal produce, tying them to autumn harvest celebrations in 2023. It features expert advice from several named canners, farmers, chefs and dietitians, covering ingredient selection, gourmet preserves, fermentation science and tools. It concludes that artisanal preservation is a growing trend heading into 2024.
one_line: A guide to canning and fermenting seasonal foods, with expert tips, gourmet trends and tools, set around autumn 2023 events.
key_facts: Canning involves placing fruits and vegetables, with spices and sometimes sugar, into jars and heating them to seal and sterilize the contents.
Sealed canned jars can be stored for months, even years, without refrigeration.
Nathaniel Thompson, a master canner and author of "Orchards in a Jar," visited the region on October 9, 2023, and said canning is "like capturing sunshine in a bottle."
Local farmer Harriet Benson launched a series of workshops on sustainable canning techniques on September 20, 2023, and advises choosing produce at peak ripeness.
Benson warns that overripe produce can give poor texture and flavor after canning, while underripe produce may never reach the correct consistency.
Julianne Clark, a chef and preservationist, introduced a line of luxury canned goods on December 1, 2023, including saffron-infused apricots and vanilla bean pear preserves.
Suggested flavor pairings for preserves include strawberry and basil and pear with thyme.

Geraldine LaRosa, a fermenter and dietitian, led a gut health seminar on November 12, 2023, and said sauerkraut, kimchi and pickles are rich in live cultures that can promote a healthy gut microbiome.
Fermentation uses beneficial bacteria or yeast to convert natural sugars into acids or alcohol, preserving food and giving it a tangy flavor.
Basic fermentation needs a jar, a sealable lid and a way to keep food submerged in brine; airlock lids and glass weights help prevent problems like mold.
Some gourmet fermenters use oak barrels or clay pots to add more complex flavors.
Chef Emilia Hammond released a collection of fermented vegetable dishes on October 25, 2023, including purple carrot kimchi and cumin-flavored beet kvass.
